validity.researcher_notes: wiki_citations.json was empty for this row (gem.wiki 403s to automated fetch this run) and every ref cell in the worklist is MISSING_REF, so there was no existing sheet citation to re-check -- this is essentially fresh research. The Iran-Pakistan-India (IPI) 'Peace Pipeline' is a very well-documented real project: a ~2,700-2,775 km, 56-inch trunk line proposed 1993/94 to move South Pars (Asaluyeh, Bushehr) gas via Pakistan (Khuzdar/Multan/Karachi corridor) to Delhi, India, at an estimated ~$7-7.5bn. India formally withdrew in 2009 (pricing/security/US pressure after the 2008 US-India nuclear deal), after which Iran and Pakistan pursued a bilateral successor ('Iran-Pakistan'/IP pipeline) that is tracked separately on gem.wiki. Confirmed independently via Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran-Pakistan_gas_pipeline), ORF (orfonline.org), Dawn (dawn.com/news/1830906), a March 2026 retrospective (insightsonindia.com), gulfoilandgas.com's project page, offshore-technology.com's project page, and a 2008 WSWS report quoting a National Iranian Gas Company official. Classification as 'transmission' is correct given the scale (56in diameter, international trunk line, 2,700+ km) even though no source uses the literal word 'transmission'. Correctly filed under GGIT gas (it is unambiguously a natural-gas pipeline, never oil/NGL). Not a phantom/GEM-only entity -- extensively covered in academic, trade-press, and government sources independent of GEM.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner1/Owner2. Every independent source that names a sponsor identifies the Iran-side entity as (National) Iranian Gas Export Company / NIGEC (offshore-technology.com: 'Iranian Gas Export Company'; other sources: NIGEC/NIGC), and the Pakistan-side sponsor as Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS), with GAIL (India) as the third original consortium member pre-2009. 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum' is at best an imprecise parent-level substitute for NIGEC (NIGEC/NIGC sits under that ministry, but is the actual named project entity everywhere in the literature -- 'Ministry of Petroleum' itself is never named as project sponsor). 'Pasargad Energy Development Co' (PEDC) has ZERO corroboration in connection with this pipeline across multiple targeted searches -- PEDC is a real Iranian company (Pasargad Bank-affiliated E&P/power firm registered April 2008) but nothing ties it to the IPI project; its later-documented deals are a 2017 NIOC oilfield development contract (Sepehr-Jufair), unrelated to this pipeline. Recommend replacing Owner1 with National Iranian Gas Export Company (NIGEC) and either dropping Owner2 pending a real source or replacing it with Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS) if the intent was to record the Pakistan-side co-sponsor.
validity.researcher_notes: Ran multiple targeted web searches for 'Pasargad Energy Development' + IPI/Iran-Pakistan-India/pipeline in every combination and found no source connecting the two. Independently, offshore-technology.com's project page for this pipeline explicitly names the sponsors as 'Iranian Gas Export Company and Inter State Gas Systems' -- neither matches either recorded Owner value. This looks like a misattribution already present in the GEM data (not something introduced this pass) and should be treated as a live data-quality defect, not a settled fact.

validity.recommendation: Minor formatting glitch, not a factual error worth an escalation: EndState/Province is recorded as 'India' (identical to EndCountryOrArea), not an actual Indian state/UT. Since the trilateral project never had a fixed final delivery point more specific than 'near Delhi/Punjab' in most sources, this may be an intentional placeholder for an unresolved sub-national endpoint rather than a data-entry slip -- flagging for a reviewer to decide whether to leave as-is or set EndState/Province to Delhi/NCT once terminus is corroborated.

fills.researcher_notes: India's withdrawal in 2009 effectively killed the trilateral IPI project; the bilateral Iran-Pakistan successor is tracked as a separate gem.wiki entity. Confirmed by 3 independent sources.
Universally described as a natural-gas pipeline sourced from South Pars; trivially confirmed.

No source uses the literal word 'transmission', but both sources describe a 56-inch, 2,700+ km international trunk gas line -- unambiguously a transmission-class pipeline, not gathering/distribution. Classification correct.

3 independent sources agree on 2009 (one lower-tier retrospective, insightsonindia.com, says India 'effectively exited negotiations in 2007' -- reflecting the gradual informal-to-formal exit, but the formal 2009 withdrawal date is the majority-sourced figure and matches GEM).

3,884.60 MMcf/d = 110 million cubic meters/day exactly. gulfoilandgas.com: 'The pipeline can carry 110 million cubic meters of gas a day' (50 mcm/d to Iran domestic use, 60 mcm/d to Pakistan). wsws.org (2008, citing a National Iranian Gas Company official): 'approximately 110 million cubic meters per day' (50 mcm/d Pakistan requirement + 60 mcm/d surplus). This total design-capacity figure matches GEM exactly and is corroborated by 2 independent sources -- initially I could not reconcile it against other sources' narrower Pakistan/India-allocation figures (60-90-150 mmscmd across different negotiation phases), but those describe country allocations, not total pipeline throughput; the 110 mcm/d total figure is the one that matches.

gulfoilandgas.com states the total route as a '2700 km pipeline'. Dawn gives a segment breakdown (Iran 1,172-1,180 km + Pakistan 705 km + India 850 km) summing to ~2,727-2,735 km, within the same range. Wikipedia/insightsonindia.com instead cite 2,775 km (1,724 mi). Length is reported inconsistently across the literature (2,700-2,775 km depending on which branch/measurement is used) -- GEM's 2,700 km falls squarely within the corroborated range and exactly matches gulfoilandgas.com, so treated as confirmed rather than a material discrepancy.
Universally cited as sourcing gas from Iran's South Pars field via the Asaluyeh terminal. Confirmed by 2+ independent sources.

StartLocation (Asaluyeh, Bushehr, Iran) and EndLocation (New Delhi/Delhi, India) both confirmed. See separate validity note flagging that EndState/Province='India' duplicates EndCountryOrArea rather than naming an actual state/UT -- likely because no source ever fixed a specific Indian sub-national terminus.

Wikipedia and offshore-technology.com both give '$7.5bn'/'US$7.5 billion' exactly matching GEM's $7,500,000,000. Other sources cite lower figures ($7bn per gulfoilandgas.com, $5.4bn per a 2008 WSWS report) -- cost estimates for this project varied over its ~20-year life and by scope (full trilateral vs. Pakistan-section-only); the two highest-quality, most-cited figures agree exactly with GEM, so treated as confirmed.

Could not corroborate either recorded owner. Every independent source that names a project sponsor points instead to National Iranian Gas Export Company / NIGEC (Iran side) and Inter State Gas Systems / ISGS (Pakistan side), with GAIL (India side) in the original trilateral form. 'Pasargad Energy Development Co' has no traceable connection to this pipeline in any source found. See paired attribution concern in validity[]. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a replacement ref for the recorded values.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is not a dormant 'proposed' project awaiting activity -- it's a terminal historical fact (India's 2009 withdrawal killed the trilateral IPI), so the dormancy/staleness rules for proposed->shelved->cancelled don't apply here; the question is only whether any later development revived or reclassified the trilateral project, and none has. Newest independent evidence found: a March 23, 2026 retrospective (insightsonindia.com) discussing the IPI purely in the past tense as a failed/superseded proposal, consistent with Wikipedia's account and with the well-known fact that Iran and Pakistan have since pursued a bilateral 'Iran-Pakistan'/IP pipeline (tracked separately) rather than reviving the trilateral India-inclusive version. No evidence of India re-entering or the trilateral project restarting. Status=cancelled / CancelledYear=2009 both confirmed as still accurate.

summary: P0451 (Iran-Pakistan-India Pipeline) is a real, extensively documented project -- confirmed cancelled/2009 (India's withdrawal) with Fuel/PipelineType/FuelSource/Length(2700km)/Capacity(3884.6 MMcf/d=110mcm/d)/SegmentCost($7.5bn) all now independently sourced at tier=high; the only defect found is on the Owner/Owner [ref] cell (Iran Ministry of Petroleum + Pasargad Energy Development Co have no independent support -- the real sponsors were NIGEC and ISGS/GAIL), flagged as an attribution concern and left UNRESOLVED, plus a minor EndState/Province='India' formatting anomaly.
